subject: Biology

stem: A model of a nucleosome contains 146 base pairs of DNA wrapped around a histone core. Samples A and B show different chromatin states.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (i) Identify the base that pairs with adenine in DNA.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) State one benefit and one limitation of molecular visualization software.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Describe how DNA and histones are organized in a nucleosome.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain how histone modification can alter transcription.

questions.title: Nucleosomes and epigenetic regulation

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (i) [1] Thymine.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [2] Benefit: permits rotation/measurement or visualization of hidden structure; limitation: model resolution/colours may not represent the real molecule or depends on input data.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: DNA is wrapped around a histone octamer; electrostatic attraction occurs between negatively charged DNA and positively charged histones; nucleosomes form repeating units connected by linker DNA.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Acetylation can loosen chromatin and increase access by transcription machinery; deacetylation/methylation can condense chromatin and reduce transcription, depending on the modification site.

stem: Two methods measured finger extension angles in 96 volunteers. The values are medians with interquartile ranges.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (i) State the dependent variable.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) Identify one feature of the dataset that should be checked before comparing methods.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Determine whether the methods give similar central values, using the data.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Evaluate the experimental design.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain why the angle changes when the finger is flexed.

questions.title: Comparing joint-angle methods

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (i) [1] Joint/finger extension angle.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [1] Outliers / skew / paired nature of measurements.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Yes; medians differ by only 1 to 2 degrees for all joints.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Strengths include a large sample and paired measurements on the same participants; limitations include no repeated measurements/blinding and an unreported age/sex distribution; improve by randomizing method order and repeating measurements.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Flexor muscles/tendons shorten and pull bones; bones rotate about the joint while antagonistic extensors relax.

stem: Impulse speed was measured in three myelinated axons from an annelid. Mean values are based on one trial per axon.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Name an instrument that displays a voltage signal against time.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (i) Distinguish standard deviation from standard error.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (ii) State a limitation of reporting one trial per axon.

parts.label: c
parts.html: (i) Calculate how many times faster axon C conducts than axon A.

parts.label: c
parts.html: (ii) Deduce the relationship between diameter and conduction speed.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain how myelin and nodes of Ranvier increase conduction speed.

questions.title: Axon diameter and conduction

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Oscilloscope / data logger with voltage-time display.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: (i) [2] Standard deviation describes spread among individual measurements; standard error estimates uncertainty in the sample mean and decreases with larger sample size.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: (ii) [1] Reliability/variation cannot be assessed and no mean or uncertainty can be estimated.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: (ii) [2] Larger diameter is associated with faster conduction; axon C has twice the diameter of A but three times the speed, so the relationship is not directly proportional.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Myelin electrically insulates the axon and reduces ion leakage; depolarization occurs mainly at nodes so the action potential appears to jump by saltatory conduction.

stem: Four beetle populations were maintained for ten generations under different selection regimes. Mean male mandible lengths were measured.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (i) Identify one improvement to the measuring equipment.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) Explain why the improvement increases data quality.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State two variables that should be controlled.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Describe the effect of selecting the smallest males, using the data.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain how the response demonstrates evolution by artificial selection.

questions.title: Selection on beetle morphology

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (i) [1] Use digital callipers/microscope graticule with finer resolution.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [2] Greater resolution reduces measurement uncertainty; repeated standardized measurements reduce random error.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Any two of starting population size, food quantity, temperature, humidity, age and sex of measured beetles.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Mean length falls from 2.42 to 1.86 mm, a decrease of 0.56 mm; controls change very little.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Mandible size varies and is heritable; selected small males reproduce disproportionately; alleles contributing to small mandibles increase in frequency across generations.
